# 4. CEK MACHINE REQUIREMENTS

Use an explicit continuation machine.

Never implement evaluation through recursive Rust calls.

Required state:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 5 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
pub struct EvalState {
    pub expr: Expr,
    pub env: Environment,
    pub continuation: Continuation,
}
```

</details>

A value is terminal only when the continuation is empty.

Never do:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
Expr::Value(v) => Halt(v)
```

</details>

without first checking the continuation.

The correct semantic structure is:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 5 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Value
 ↓
continuation empty?
 ├── yes → Halt
 └── no  → resume frame
```

</details>

---

# 5. LAMBDA / CALL REQUIREMENTS

Lambda captures the lexical environment at creation.

Calls evaluate:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 5 lines</strong></summary>

```text
function
argument 0
argument 1
...
argument N
```

</details>

strictly left-to-right.

Arity mismatch is detected immediately after function evaluation and BEFORE any argument evaluation.

Application uses the captured closure environment.

Caller environment and closure environment must remain distinct.

Required tests:

- lexical capture;
- shadowing;
- left-to-right argument ordering;
- arity precheck;
- non-function call;
- deep call stack;
- continuation serialization;
- resume equivalence.

---

# 6. CAPABILITY KERNEL REQUIREMENTS

Capabilities use opaque generation-safe references.

Authority remains substrate-private.

Derivation:

\[
derive(A,C)\preceq A
\]

must always hold.

Authorization is effect-specific:

\[
Authorized(A,E,t)
\]

requires:

- operation;
- target scope;
- parameter constraint;
- resource ceiling;
- lifetime;
- explicit logical time.

Revocation of an ancestor invalidates descendants.

No raw capability authority may cross an ordinary actor message.

---

# 7. BUDGET REQUIREMENTS

Consumables:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```text
fuel
I/O
duration
```

</details>

Reserved resources:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 2 lines</strong></summary>

```text
memory
concurrency slots
```

</details>

Deadline:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```text
absolute W
```

</details>

Never use saturating subtraction.

Use checked arithmetic.

Maintain:

\[
C_{available}+C_{escrowed}+C_{consumed}=C_{initial}
\]

and:

\[
R_n=R_0+\sum reserve_i-\sum release_i
\]

Effect completion cost is escrowed at issuance so completion accounting cannot fail due to budget exhaustion.

---

# 8. EFFECT REQUEST REQUIREMENTS

The Request sequence is immutable:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 16 lines</strong></summary>

```text
1. evaluate capability
2. evaluate target
3. evaluate arguments left-to-right
4. construct canonical Effect
5. validate capability
6. authorize exact effect
7. capability ceiling
8. runtime budget
9. runtime reservation
10. deadline
11. host policy
12. allocate EffectId
13. commit issue budget/reservation
14. durable issuance
15. Pending
16. host invocation
```

</details>

No host call before durable issuance.

Required invariant:

\[
HostInvoked(E)\Rightarrow DurableIssued(E)
\]

Receipt must validate both:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 2 lines</strong></summary>

```text
EffectId
EffectDigest
```

</details>

A corrupted receipt must never resume the actor.

---

# 9. ACTOR REQUIREMENTS

Actors provide concurrency without semantic nondeterminism.

Scheduler:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```text
FIFO
one actor per queue position
one CEK transition per scheduler turn
```

</details>

Pending, Blocked, Halted, and Faulted actors are never scheduled.

Actors have isolated:

- heaps;
- environments;
- continuations;
- mailboxes;
- budgets;
- capability contexts.

Spawn is budget transfer, not budget creation.

Child actors receive explicitly derived capabilities only.

---

# 10. MARSHALLING REQUIREMENTS

Ordinary data marshalling must reject capabilities recursively.

This includes capabilities nested inside:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 4 lines</strong></summary>

```text
List
Tuple
Function
nested structures
```

</details>

Raw `CapRef` transfer is forbidden.

Authority crosses actor boundaries only through explicit delegation.

Delegation must invoke the capability kernel and preserve:

\[
DelegatedAuthority\preceq ParentAuthority
\]

---

# 11. CANONICAL SERIALIZATION REQUIREMENTS

Phase 15A is frozen.

Canonical envelope:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 4 lines</strong></summary>

```text
version: u8
type_tag: u8
payload_length: u32 BE
payload
```

</details>

Do not use Rust struct layout.

Do not use `bincode` as the canonical semantic format.

All lengths and arithmetic must be checked.

No attacker-controlled preallocation from encoded collection counts.

Maps MUST reject duplicate keys.

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
if map.insert(key, value).is_some() {
    return Err(CanonicalError::DuplicateMapKey);
}
```

</details>

Malformed input must produce explicit errors.

Trailing bytes must be rejected.

Nested decoding must use bounded cursors.

---

# 12. PERSISTENCE REQUIREMENTS

Persistence framing must never redefine semantic serialization.

Architecture:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 5 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Phase 15A canonical bytes
        ↓
Persistence framing
        ↓
WAL / snapshot / effect journal
```

</details>

Required effect causality:

\[
Issued\Rightarrow Prepared
\]

\[
Completed\Rightarrow Issued
\]

\[
Reconciled\Rightarrow Issued
\]

Required durability boundary:

\[
HostInvoked(E)\Rightarrow DurableIssued(E)
\]

Prepared-only transactions are discarded.

Issued-but-not-completed effects are:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Indeterminate
```

</details>

never automatically:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```text
NotExecuted
```

</details>

# 13. SNAPSHOT REQUIREMENTS

A snapshot is valid iff:

\[
ValidSnapshot(S)
\iff
Commit(S)
\land
Digest(Canonical(S))=RecordedDigest(S)
\]

Partial snapshots are garbage.

Recovery must never silently repair:

- sequence gaps;
- checksum corruption;
- budget inconsistencies;
- invalid actor tables;
- duplicate runnable actors;
- invalid continuation state;
- effect journal causality violations.

Invalid state produces `RecoveryFault`.

For every request:

<details>

```text
expected EffectDigest
```

must match the next trace entry.

# 28. PROHIBITED SHORTCUTS

Never:

- use recursive evaluation;
- trust AST shape as a security boundary;
- expose authority internals;
- clone capabilities wholesale during spawn;
- transfer raw capability references through ordinary messages;
- use wall-clock time for deterministic semantics;
- use saturating budget arithmetic;
- invoke host before durable issuance;
- infer external-effect nonexecution from missing completion;
- silently repair persistence corruption;
- use production recovery as the reference recovery oracle;
- use production serialization as the reference serialization oracle;
- compare only final return values;
- accept surviving mutations without adjudication;
- reduce semantic coverage to satisfy CI timing;
- weaken tests because implementation is inconvenient.

---

# 29. FINAL ACCEPTANCE CONDITION

The implementation is not considered conformant merely because unit tests pass.

The engineering standard is:

\[
\boxed{
Observe_P(X)=Observe_R(X)
}
\]

over the tested state space,

together with:

\[
\boxed{
MutationKillRate=100\%
}
\]

for all non-equivalent registered mutations,

and:

\[
\boxed{
Canonical(Recover_P(D))
=
Canonical(Recover_R(D))
}
\]

for the tested persistence state space, subject to authoritative external-effect reconciliation.

The final claim must remain:

> **Let the independent reference model, exhaustive/property-based tests, mutation testing, and crash-injection suite provide machine-checked evidence that the implementation conforms to the frozen calculus over the tested state space.**

Do not claim more than the evidence establishes.

---

# 30. START CONDITION

The architecture is frozen.

Do not propose another semantic phase.

Begin implementation from the lowest dependency layer, establish the independent reference model alongside the production implementation, and keep the differential harness operational as early as possible.

Your primary objective is to make it:

```text
deterministic
```

The repository must make the following architectural property difficult to violate accidentally:

\[
\boxed{
Untrusted\ Input
\not\Rightarrow
Authority
\not\Rightarrow
External\ Effect
}

and:

\[
\boxed{
Production\ Semantics
\neq
Reference\ Implementation
}

while independently maintaining:

<details>

# 16. Visibility Rules

Default to private.

Use:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
pub(crate)
```

</details>

for trusted internal boundaries.

Use:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
pub
```

</details>

only when an API is intentionally part of the crate's external contract.

Examples:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
pub struct CapRef { ... }
```

</details>

may be public.

But:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
pub struct AuthorityNode { ... }
```

</details>

must NOT be public.

Likewise:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
pub(crate) fn finalize(...)
```

</details>

for executable-plan construction.

# 17. ExecutablePlan Construction Boundary

The runtime must never be able to construct an executable plan directly from arbitrary language data.

Preferred structure:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 5 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
pub struct ExecutablePlan {
    ir: PlanIR,
    bounds: ResourceBounds,
    _sealed: Sealed,
}
```

</details>

where construction is restricted to the compiler.

The runtime accepts:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
fn execute(plan: &ExecutablePlan)
```

</details>

not:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
fn execute(block: &Block)
```

</details>

This distinction is mandatory.

---

# 18. Capability Boundary

Production code must use:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
CapRef
```

</details>

rather than passing authority structures.

Authority storage remains internal to the kernel.

The runtime can request:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
kernel.validate(...)
kernel.authorize(...)
kernel.derive(...)
```

</details>

but cannot inspect:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 6 lines</strong></summary>

```text
scope
parameters
resource ceiling
lifetime
parent authority
revocation state
```

</details>

directly.

---

# 19. Host Boundary

No evaluator module may import:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
std::fs
std::net
std::process
```

</details>

or equivalent host-effect APIs.

External effects must flow through:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 15 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Expr::Request
      ↓
Effect
      ↓
Capability gate
      ↓
Budget gate
      ↓
Deadline gate
      ↓
HostPolicy
      ↓
Durable issuance
      ↓
HostExecutor
```

</details>

This is an architectural rule, not merely a coding convention.

---

# 20. Persistence Boundary

No runtime transition should directly perform arbitrary persistence I/O.

Use a persistence interface:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (rust) — 7 lines</strong></summary>

```rust
pub trait Persistence {
    fn append(&mut self, record: WalRecord)
        -> Result<(), PersistenceError>;

    fn sync(&mut self)
        -> Result<(), PersistenceError>;
}
```

</details>

The machine determines the semantic transition.

The persistence layer determines how that transition becomes durable.

---

# 21. Phase 15A Bootstrap

Before building the full runtime, implement canonical serialization.

Initial files:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 9 lines</strong></summary>

```text
ror-core/
└── src/
    ├── canonical/
    │   ├── mod.rs
    │   ├── encode.rs
    │   ├── decode.rs
    │   ├── cursor.rs
    │   ├── error.rs
    │   └── tags.rs
```

Implement:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 6 lines</strong></summary>

```text
CanonicalPayload
CanonicalEncode
CanonicalDecode
ReadCursor
envelope()
checked_length()
```

</details>

Required vectors:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Symbol(1)
Value::Symbol(Symbol(1))
Map(Symbol(1) → false, Symbol(2) → true)
```

</details>

Required rejection cases:

<details>

```text

wrong type tag

length overflow
```

</details>

# 22. Phase 15A Golden Vector Policy

Golden vectors live outside implementation source:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 1 lines</strong></summary>


Each vector should include:

<details>

```text
name
```

# 23. Independent Reference Requirement

The reference model should be written early.

Do not postpone it until production is “complete.”

Preferred development sequence:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 9 lines</strong></summary>

```text
production component
       ↓
reference component
       ↓
differential test
       ↓
mutation test
       ↓
next component
```

</details>

This minimizes the possibility that production implementation decisions silently become the specification.

<details>

```text
        ↕
```

# 25. Test Organization

Unit tests stay close to their implementation.

Integration tests live under:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```text
tests/
```

</details>

Recommended:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 6 lines</strong></summary>

```text
tests/conformance/
tests/exhaustive/
tests/property/
tests/mutation/
tests/crash/
tests/stress/
```

</details>

The separation is intentional.

A unit test answers:

> Does this local component behave correctly?

A differential test answers:

> Does production agree with the independent semantics?

A mutation test answers:

> Can the verification system detect a known semantic defect?

A crash test answers:

> Does durability/recovery preserve the frozen machine semantics?

---

# 26. Feature Flags

Avoid semantic feature flags.

Do not create:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```text
feature = "legacy-call-order"
feature = "unsafe-capabilities"
feature = "old-budget"
```

</details>

Frozen semantics should have one implementation.

Development-only instrumentation may use features, for example:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```text
feature = "trace-debug"
feature = "mutation"
feature = "stress"
```

</details>

but these must not alter normal semantic behavior.

---

# 27. Unsafe Rust Policy

Default policy:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```text
#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
```

</details>

at crate level unless a concrete implementation requirement demonstrates that `unsafe` is necessary.

Any future `unsafe` must have:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 5 lines</strong></summary>

```text
reason
invariant
safety proof
tests
review
```

</details>

and must not weaken the capability/effect boundary.

The initial implementation should remain entirely safe Rust where practical.

---

# 28. Panic Policy

Trusted runtime code must not use panic as normal semantic control flow.

Recoverable conditions become explicit errors/faults.

Especially:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 8 lines</strong></summary>

```text
budget underflow
invalid capability
invalid receipt
corrupt WAL
sequence gap
invalid snapshot
marshal failure
host failure
```

</details>

must not be represented by accidental panics.

`unwrap()` and `expect()` should be restricted to statically justified invariants and reviewed individually.

---

# 29. Determinism Rules

Never depend on:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 7 lines</strong></summary>

```text
HashMap iteration order
OS scheduling
thread ID
memory address
wall-clock time
random allocator behavior
unordered host completion
```

</details>

where semantic determinism matters.

Use deterministic structures such as:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 6 lines</strong></summary>

```text
BTreeMap
BTreeSet
VecDeque
explicit IDs
explicit logical time
ordered traces
```

</details>

Randomized testing is allowed.

Randomness must be an explicit test input, never hidden machine state.

---

# 30. Initial Error Taxonomy

Keep errors semantically distinct.

Actor-local:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 7 lines</strong></summary>

```text
ArityMismatch
TypeError
BudgetExhausted
CapabilityDenied
MarshalFault
HostFault
ReplayCorruption
```

</details>

Global:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 8 lines</strong></summary>

```text
SnapshotCorruption
EventLogCorruption
EventSequenceGap
InvalidRecoveredState
EffectReconciliationFailure
PersistenceFailure
ActorTableCorruption
SchedulerInvariantViolation
```

</details>

Do not collapse all failures into a generic `RuntimeError`.

Create:

Example:

```toml
[[obligation]]

[[obligation]]
```

:::writing{variant="document" id="31684"}
# Red-on-Rust

**A deterministic, capability-scoped, resource-bounded, crash-recoverable execution machine for probabilistically generated programs.**

Red-on-Rust is a Rust-based execution substrate for a family of homoiconic, dialect-oriented languages inspired by the compositional model of the REBOL/Red lineage.

Its purpose is not merely to execute generated programs safely.

Its purpose is to establish a **small, explicit, deterministic machine boundary** between probabilistic program generation and consequential computation.

---

## Status

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 5 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Architecture:       FROZEN
Specification:      FROZEN
Verification:       FROZEN
Repository:         BOOTSTRAP
Implementation:     IN PROGRESS
```

</details>

> **Frozen specification ≠ verified implementation.**

The architecture defines required behavior. Independent reference execution, differential testing, mutation testing, crash injection, stress testing, and security review provide the evidence that an implementation conforms to that specification.

---

# Core Thesis

> **Red-on-Rust is a deterministic, capability-scoped, resource-bounded, crash-recoverable execution machine for probabilistically generated programs.**

The central security boundary is the machine, not the language surface and not the model generating the program.

The fundamental property is:

\[
\boxed{
LLMOutput\land UntrustedInput\not\Rightarrow ExternalEffect
}
\]

An external effect requires the complete chain of validation, authority, resource, policy, durability, and issuance checks.

\[
\boxed{
ExternalEffect(E)
\Rightarrow
ValidatedPlan(P)
\land Authorized(E,\kappa,t)
\land CapabilityWithinCeiling(E)
\land BudgetAvailable(E)
\land DeadlineValid(E,t)
\land HostPolicyOK(E)
\land Issued(E)
}
\]

---

# Architecture

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 36 lines</strong></summary>

```text
                    UNTRUSTED
                       │
                ┌──────▼──────┐
                │ LLM /       │
                │ Planner     │
                └──────┬──────┘
                       │
                  PlanProposal
                       │
                ┌──────▼──────┐
                │ Compiler    │
                │ parse       │
                │ validate    │
                │ lower       │
                └──────┬──────┘
                       │
                 ExecutablePlan
                       │
                ┌──────▼──────┐
                │ CEK Machine │
                └───┬─────┬───┘
                    │     │
             ┌──────▼┐   ┌▼────────┐
             │Capability│ │ Budget │
             │ Kernel   │ │ System │
             └──────┬──┘ └───┬────┘
                    │        │
                    └────┬───┘
                         │
                  Effect Issuance
                         │
                  Durable Boundary
                         │
                    ┌────▼────┐
                    │  Host   │
                    └─────────┘
```

</details>

The verification architecture is independent:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 7 lines</strong></summary>

```text
             Production
                  │
                  ▼
            Observation
                  ▲
                  │
             Reference
```

</details>

The production implementation and executable reference model do not share core transition logic.

---

# Design Principles

## 1. The LLM is untrusted

The planner generates proposals.

It does not possess authority.

It cannot directly:

- allocate capabilities;
- authorize effects;
- modify budgets;
- modify scheduler state;
- allocate actors;
- invoke the host;
- bypass compilation;
- bypass persistence.

The machine evaluates the proposal after validation.

---

## 2. `Block` is not executable authority

The language representation is untrusted data.

The compiler transforms it through:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 15 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Block
  ↓
parse
  ↓
normalize
  ↓
validate
  ↓
lower
  ↓
capability analysis
  ↓
resource analysis
  ↓
ExecutablePlan
```

</details>

Critically:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Block ≠ ExecutablePlan
```

</details>

Only validated executable plans enter the trusted machine.

---

## 3. Explicit CEK execution

Evaluation uses an explicit CEK-style machine:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Control
Environment
Continuation
```

</details>

The evaluator does not depend on recursive host-language calls for semantic call-stack management.

This makes continuation state explicit, serializable, replayable, and recoverable.

A value is terminal only when its continuation is empty.

---

## 4. Capability-based authority

Authority is represented by opaque capability references.

The evaluator cannot inspect authority internals.

Capabilities can be:

- attenuated;
- constrained;
- revoked;
- expired;
- scoped to operations;
- scoped to targets;
- constrained by parameters;
- bounded by resources;
- bounded by lifetime.

Derivation satisfies:

\[
\boxed{
derive(A,C)\preceq A
}
\]

No authority amplification is permitted.

---

## 5. Resource-bounded execution

Execution is bounded by multiple dimensions.

Consumables:

\[
C=\langle F,I,D\rangle
\]

where:

- \(F\) = fuel;
- \(I\) = I/O units;
- \(D\) = duration budget.

Reserved resources:

\[
R=\langle M,S\rangle
\]

where:

- \(M\) = memory;
- \(S\) = concurrency slots.

A deadline is an absolute logical-time bound.

Budget conservation is explicit:

\[
C_{available}+C_{escrowed}+C_{consumed}=C_{initial}
\]

Checked arithmetic is required.

Saturating subtraction is not used for semantic accounting.

---

## 6. Effects are explicit and transactional

External effects are represented as canonical effect descriptions.

A request passes through:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 19 lines</strong></summary>

```text
capability evaluation
        ↓
target evaluation
        ↓
argument evaluation
        ↓
canonical Effect
        ↓
capability authorization
        ↓
resource checks
        ↓
deadline check
        ↓
host policy
        ↓
durable issuance
        ↓
host invocation
```

</details>

The critical durability invariant is:

\[
\boxed{
HostInvoked(E)\Rightarrow DurableIssued(E)
}
\]

An effect is not considered merely "issued" because an in-memory object exists.

---

## 7. Actors provide concurrency, not semantic nondeterminism

Actors have isolated:

- environments;
- continuations;
- heaps;
- mailboxes;
- budgets;
- capability contexts.

The scheduler is deterministic.

The baseline scheduler is FIFO with one CEK transition per actor turn.

Therefore:

\[
InitialState + SchedulerTrace + HostTrace
\Rightarrow UniqueMachineTrace
\]

---

## 8. Authority does not cross ordinary message boundaries

Ordinary marshalling recursively rejects capabilities.

Raw capability references cannot simply be copied from one actor to another.

Authority transfer requires explicit delegation through the capability kernel.

Thus ordinary data transfer does not amplify receiver authority.

---

## 9. Canonical serialization

Semantic serialization is explicit and independent of Rust memory layout.

The canonical envelope is:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 4 lines</strong></summary>

```text
version:        u8
type_tag:       u8
payload_length: u32 BE
payload:        bytes
```

</details>

Canonical encoding defines semantic identity.

It is not based on `bincode`, struct layout, pointer addresses, allocator behavior, or platform-specific representation.

Malformed encodings are rejected.

Duplicate map keys are rejected.

Trailing bytes are rejected.

Encoded collection counts do not authorize attacker-controlled preallocation.

---

## 10. Crash recovery is causal

Persistence consists of:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 5 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Snapshot
   +
WAL
   +
Effect Journal
```

</details>

Effect lifecycle:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 5 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Prepared
   ↓
Issued
   ↓
Completed
```

</details>

or:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Issued
   ↓
Reconciled
```

</details>

A prepared-but-never-issued effect is discarded.

An issued-but-not-completed effect is:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 1 lines</strong></summary>

```text
Indeterminate
```

</details>

unless an authoritative host reconciliation protocol establishes its outcome.

The system never infers "not executed" merely because a completion record is missing.

# Trust Model

| Component | Trust | Role |
|---|---:|---|
| LLM / planner | No | Proposal generation |
| `Block` | No | Untrusted program data |
| Compiler | Yes | Executable invariants |
| Capability kernel | Yes | Authority decisions |
| CEK machine | Yes | Deterministic execution |
| Scheduler | Yes | Deterministic interleaving |
| Budget system | Yes | Resource conservation |
| Persistence | Yes | Durable machine state |
| Effect journal | Yes | Causal effect state |
| Replay host | Yes | Recorded-effect reconstruction |
| Live host | Partial | External-world execution |
| Supervisor | Yes | Lifecycle and recovery |

The trusted computing base is intentionally explicit.

# Verification Strategy

Red-on-Rust does not rely on a single testing technique.

## Independent reference model

The reference implementation independently models:

- CEK evaluation;
- lexical environments;
- closures;
- calls;
- capability derivation;
- revocation;
- budgets;
- actors;
- scheduling;
- effects;
- persistence;
- recovery.

Production and reference implementations are compared through normalized semantic observations.

---

## Differential testing

The principal semantic oracle is:

\[
\boxed{
Observe(Production(X))
=
Observe(Reference(X))
}
\]

The comparator reports the first divergence.

Internal implementation details such as memory addresses and Rust layout are excluded unless semantically relevant.

---

## Exhaustive testing

Small-state enumeration covers the frozen calculus over bounded state spaces.

Baseline targets include:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 3 lines</strong></summary>

```text
expression depth ≤ 4
actors ≤ 2
capabilities ≤ 2
```

</details>

CI performance limits are treated as engineering budgets, not reasons to reduce semantic coverage.

---

## Property-based testing

Randomized tests exercise larger generated state spaces.

Every test is reproducible from an explicit seed and versioned generator metadata.

---

## Mutation testing

Known semantic defects are deliberately injected.

Examples include:

- reversing argument evaluation order;
- skipping arity checks;
- accepting revoked capabilities;
- amplifying authority;
- omitting budget gates;
- releasing indeterminate effect escrow;
- scheduling blocked actors;
- accepting duplicate runnable entries;
- ignoring WAL gaps;
- accepting checksum failures;
- accepting mismatched effect digests.

The target is:

\[
\boxed{
MutationKillRate=100\%
}
\]

for all registered non-equivalent mutations.

---

## Crash testing

The effect protocol is tested at:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 7 lines</strong></summary>

```text
T0 BeforePrepared
T1 AfterPrepared
T2 AfterIssued
T3 AfterHostInvocation
T4 AfterHostCompletion
T5 AfterCompleted
T6 AfterSnapshotCommit
```

</details>

Recovery must preserve the frozen causal semantics at every crash point.

---

# Verification Contract

Every frozen requirement receives a stable obligation ID.

Examples:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 19 lines</strong></summary>

```text
CEK-CALL-ARITY-PRECHECK
CEK-CALL-ARGS-LTR
CEK-CLOSURE-LEXICAL-CAPTURE

CAP-DERIVE-NO-AMPLIFICATION
CAP-REVOCATION-ANCESTOR

BUDGET-ESCROW-CONSERVATION

EFFECT-ISSUE-DURABLE-BEFORE-HOST
EFFECT-RECEIPT-DIGEST-VALIDATION

SCHED-FIFO
SCHED-BLOCKED-NOT-SCHEDULED

MARSHAL-CAPABILITY-REJECT

WAL-GAP-REJECT
RECOVERY-ISSUED-INDETERMINATE
```

</details>

Coverage metrics are evidence.

They do not replace differential agreement.

---

# Reproducible Counterexamples

A failed generated case records:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 12 lines</strong></summary>

```text
seed
generator_version
semantic_version
test_case_version
accepted_plan_trace
scheduler_trace
host_trace
crash_trace
minimized_input
production_observation
reference_observation
first_divergence
```

</details>

Every failure should be reproducible locally.

Divergences are classified as:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 4 lines</strong></summary>

```text
production defect
reference defect
harness defect
specification ambiguity
```

</details>

Specification ambiguity must be resolved explicitly rather than hidden in a test adjustment.

# Security Invariants

The implementation is designed around several non-negotiable invariants.

### No unauthorized external effects

\[
\boxed{
\neg Authorized(E,\kappa,t)
\Rightarrow
\neg ExternalEffect(E)
}
\]

### No authority amplification

\[
\boxed{
derive(A,C)\preceq A
}
\]

### No budget teleportation

\[
\boxed{
C_{available}+C_{escrowed}+C_{consumed}=C_{initial}
}
\]

### No host-before-durability

\[
\boxed{
HostInvoked(E)\Rightarrow DurableIssued(E)
}
\]

### No raw capability transfer

\[
\boxed{
OrdinaryMarshal(Value::Capability)
=
Rejected
}
\]

### No silent recovery corruption

Invalid persistence state produces an explicit recovery fault.

It is never silently repaired by mutation.

```text
20. Stress / security validation
```

</details>

The independent reference model and differential infrastructure should be established as early as practical rather than postponed until the production runtime is complete.

---

# Engineering Rules

The following shortcuts are prohibited:

- recursive evaluator implementation;
- hidden authority inspection;
- implicit capability creation;
- wholesale capability copying;
- raw capability transfer through ordinary messages;
- saturating resource subtraction;
- wall-clock time as semantic machine state;
- host invocation before durable issuance;
- treating incomplete effects as automatically unexecuted;
- silent persistence repair;
- unordered replay;
- production/reference implementation reuse;
- comparing only final return values;
- weakening tests to accommodate implementation convenience.

# Conformance Claim

The project deliberately avoids claiming that test execution constitutes a mathematical proof of the entire calculus.

The appropriate engineering claim is:

> **The independent reference model, exhaustive/property-based tests, mutation testing, and crash-injection suite provide machine-checked evidence that the implementation conforms to the frozen calculus over the tested state space.**

Formal mechanization may provide stronger guarantees in the future, but it is not required to begin implementation.

---

# Why Red-on-Rust?

Probabilistic systems can generate useful programs.

They should not receive implicit authority merely because those programs look plausible.

Red-on-Rust therefore separates:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 27 lines</strong></summary>

```text
generation
from
validation

validation
from
execution

execution
from
authority

authority
from
resources

resources
from
external effects

external effects
from
durability

durability
from
recovery
```

</details>

The resulting machine is intended to make consequential computation:

<details>
<summary><strong>💻 Code Block (text) — 6 lines</strong></summary>

```text
explicit
bounded
authorized
deterministic
observable
recoverable
```

</details>

while retaining a highly compositional, homoiconic programming model above the substrate.
